title: update and the pointer grammar
description: User story under REQ-173. Every ledger supports `update <id>` with field patches validated as `add` validates; `resolvedBy` on a brief statement is a closed pointer grammar validated by D2.
iWant: to patch a statement's kind, text or resolution
soThat: a correction does not mint a duplicate

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] given statement 7, when rcf define ledger brief update 7 --kind constraint --resolved-by REQ-003 runs, then the statement carries kind constraint and resolvedBy REQ-003 and its id and addedAt are unchanged.
[happy] given decision 2 with one option, when rcf define ledger decisions update 2 --option a:x --option b:y --default a runs, then decisions:wellFormed passes it.

[happy] given each pointer form REQ-nnn, TAD.entity:<name>, PRD.user:<name>, TAD.system:<name>, TAC-nnnn and omitted:<reason> resolving on the fixture, when D2 runs, then skeleton:resolvedBy passes the statement.
[failure] given --resolved-by "loan thing", when update runs, then it exits 2 naming the grammar and writes nothing.
[failure] given --resolved-by REQ-999 on a tree with no REQ-999, when D2 runs, then skeleton:resolvedBy fails the statement with "pointer does not resolve".
[must-not] given a statement whose text contains an existing REQ title and no resolvedBy, when D2 runs in 0.30.0, then skeleton:resolvedBy does not pass it on the title hit.

[happy] (R1 2026-10-05) given rcf define ledger brief add --id 3 --text "foo" --kind capability on a ledger whose entry 3 already carries kind capability and text foo, when the verb runs, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'brief-ledger: unchanged 3' (with --json, {"status":"unchanged","id":3}); the file is not rewritten.

[failure] (R1 2026-10-05) given rcf define ledger brief add --id 3 --text "bar" --kind constraint on a ledger whose entry 3 carries kind capability and text foo, when the verb runs, then it exits 3 and stderr names the id and the differing fields (text, kind); the file is not rewritten.

[happy] (R1 2026-10-05) given rcf define ledger brief add --text "foo" with no --id on an empty ledger, when the verb runs, then it mints id 1 as before (idempotency opt-in is id-carried; the harness threads --id back on replay).

[happy] (R1 create extension 2026-10-05, PR 292 follow-up) given rcf define create ac --parent US-1 --id AC-1-1 --description "foo" on a tree where AC-1-1 already carries description "foo" with its parent US-1, when the verb runs, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'AC-1-1: unchanged' (with --json emitting {"status":"unchanged","id":"AC-1-1","filePath":"rcf/.../ac/ac-1-1.json"}); the file is not rewritten; and given the same verb with --description "bar" instead, it exits 3 and stderr names the id and the differing fields (description); the file is not rewritten.
